ilse_first_meet: ^A Grey Sister sits on the Shrine's step with a writing board on her knees, copying from a tablet so worn it is mostly guesswork. She frowns at the guesswork.
^"Sister Ilse. Reedholm sent me up to write down whatever comes out of the barrows before somebody burns it or sells it."

b: ^"You were at Reedholm. I know the way you're standing: like someone waiting to be told off for reading at table. Sit. Nobody here will tell you off."
^"The Company burned a library at Ashgate. I don't hold you to it. I hold them to it."
^"You're from here. Then you'll know the barrows were quiet your whole life. They aren't now. Somebody should write down why."
^"The Deepdelvers keep records in stone. It's a good habit. It's also why nobody reads them."
^"You'll be going down there. Everyone is, now."

s0: ^Ilse looks up from the board and holds up a finger until she finishes the word.
s1: ^. Anything with writing on it today?"
s2: ^"The Shrine's quiet. The quiet is the nice part."

ilse_greet_fallen: ^." She puts the board down. "The Shrine can raise them. Go in. I'll wait."
ilse_writing: ^"The Chronicle. Anything the old empire left that still says something: orders, rolls, letters. One to three lines, usually. They didn't write for us."
^"Put enough of them in order and they stop being scraps and start being a sentence. Then you find out whether you wanted to read it."
ilse_look: ^"Anything with a stamp or a name. The barrows' chests, the old shrines down there, and the halls at the foot of each stair. The dead kept their best things where they kept their best men."
^"Don't guess what it says. Bring it to me. I'll guess properly."

s1: ^"Mind your feet on the stairs down there. They're older than they look."
s2: ^Ilse has already bent back over the tablet.
